nghi_van.mo_ta: A modern airliner, a twin-engine jet, flies over the bay.
nghi_van.ly_do: Jet aircraft did not exist in 1780. Powered flight began in 1903 and jet airliners in the 1950s.

tra_loi.vat: A twin-engine jet airliner in flight
tra_loi.dac_diem: It has a white fuselage and swept-back wings. One engine is visible under the wing. The tail fin is blue with a round emblem. It is seen from the side against a pale blue sky with thin clouds, and the sea horizon is at the bottom.
tra_loi.ly_do: Jet airliners first flew in the 1950s. Powered aircraft of any kind did not exist until 1903. In 1780 the only aircraft were hot-air and hydrogen balloons, and the first of those flew in 1783.

nghi_van.mo_ta: A red modern convertible car is parked on a dirt track on the hillside.
nghi_van.ly_do: Motor cars did not exist in 1780. The first petrol car was built in 1885, and this body style is 21st-century.

tra_loi.vat: A red convertible passenger car (modern motor vehicle) on a dirt track on a hillside
tra_loi.dac_diem: Red glossy body, low roofless convertible shape, alloy wheels, front headlights and grille, licence plate at the front. It sits on a dusty track across a scrubby slope. A steel electricity pylon with power lines stands on the ridge behind it.
tra_loi.ly_do: Petrol-engined cars date from about 1886, and this is a modern convertible design. Nothing like it existed in 1780, when transport was horse-drawn carts and carriages. The pylon is also anachronistic.

nghi_van.mo_ta: A steel lattice electricity pylon with overhead power lines stands on the ridge.
nghi_van.ly_do: High-voltage transmission pylons and power lines are 20th-century infrastructure. Electrical grids did not exist in 1780.

tra_loi.vat: Electricity transmission pylon with overhead power lines
tra_loi.dac_diem: Tall steel lattice tower on a hill crest, with cross-arms on both sides. Several conductor wires run off to the left and right. It stands against the sky. A red modern car is visible on the slope below.
tra_loi.ly_do: Steel lattice high-voltage pylons and power lines only appeared in the late 19th and early 20th century. Nothing like them existed in 1780.
